chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Hammad, from Al-Halabi, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

I asked him about a man who divorces his wife while he is absent from her, from which day should she observe the waiting period? He said: If she establishes just proof that she was divorced on a known day, and she is convinced, let her observe the waiting period from the day she was divorced; and if she did not preserve [the knowledge] of which day and which month, let her observe the waiting period from the day it reaches her.
ai.seo_question: How does a woman observe her waiting period if her husband is absent and she does not know the exact day of divorce?
ai.summary: Recorded in al-Kafi, this hadith from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) establishes the jurisprudential principle that the iddah commences upon the actual occurrence of the divorce if proven, rather than merely upon notification, highlighting the Shia emphasis on substantive legal reality over procedural delay. It underscores the importance of evidentiary standards ('bayyinat al-adl') in family law, ensuring that the woman's rights are protected against uncertainty regarding the timing of the marital dissolution.
